display.title: Episode 136: The Dike (Tisha B'Av)
display.summary_short: On Tisha B'Av: Torah, davening and kindness as a summer 'diet' for the soul, the story of a lost girl brought home by the light of Shabbos candles, and the ancient tune of Eichah.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Tisha B'Av. Uncle Yossi talks about rebuilding the Beis HaMikdash through three things: Torah, which lights up the world and shows right from wrong, so set a time to learn each day of the summer; avodah, davening to Hashem, who alone grants every need, as the Rambam taught; and gemilus chasadim, above all daily tzedakah, which helps the poor and refines the giver. A first-grade boy leads the Shema. The story takes place in a Dutch town by the sea. Kind Leah nurses her mischievous little sister Gittel after a fall. One day the dike breaks and everyone flees the flood, but Gittel falls behind. A hard, cruel old woman carries her to her cottage, tells her she has no family left, and works her for three years until she forgets her home and that she is Jewish. Sent to a distant fair, Gittel walks home after dark and sees Shabbos candles glowing in a window. Memories flood back; she knocks, and the door is opened by her sister. The show closes by explaining that the sad tune of Eichah, sung through the long exile, carries hope, and with a prayer that Tisha B'Av become a Yom Tov.
display.lesson: The light of Shabbos candles can bring a Jewish child home; and Torah, prayer and kindness keep the soul strong and help rebuild the Beis HaMikdash.

date.note: 'Today is Tisha B'Av, a fast day'; 9 Av 5744 was Tuesday 7 August 1984, weekly from 133 (17 Tammuz).

advisories.note: A dike breaks and a little girl is left asleep in the path of the flood.
A cruel woman keeps the girl for three years, tells her she has no family, works her hard and threatens beatings.
A child separated from her family forgets her home and her Jewishness before the happy reunion.
Tisha B'Av and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.

sources_cited.note: Attributed to the Rambam: whatever you need, turn only to Hashem.
'Az yashir' read as 'will sing': the song of the Geulah, as 'our Chachamim tell us'.
